text: וְיִגְעֲלָם. בְּרִית לִזְכֹּר: זְכֹר נְקוּבֵי מַטּוֹת. שְׁבוּעוֹת מַטּוֹת. נְדִידוֹת הַמַּטּוֹת. לְאַמְּצָם יִזְכֹּר: נוֹשְׂאֵי עֹל מוֹטוֹת. אִם פֶּץ לַחֲמוֹטוֹת. נִיַּץ חֲדַר הַמִּטּוֹת. לְכַפֵּר יִזְכֹּר: זְכֹר מְצוּקִים. יְסוֹד מוּצָקִים. מְפַעֲלִים לְיֹצְקִים. בְּכוֹם חוּשׁ לִזְכֹּר: מִפִּי יוֹנְקִים. אֲשֶׁר בְּסוּף נוֹאֲקִים. מַאֲמַר בְּרִית וְהַחֻקִּים. דְּבַר קָדְשׁוֹ יִזְכֹּר: זְכֹר לֵין כְּפָרִים. וְאִמְרֵי שְׁפָרִים. לִמְשַׁלְּמֵי פָרִים. לִפְלֵאָה יִזְכֹּר: לְעֵת בִּקּוּר כְּפוּרִים. סְתוּרִים מְסַפְּרִים. לִשְׁנֵי עֳפָרִים. לְצֶדֶק יִזְכֹּר: זְכֹר כְּבוֹד מִשְׁכָּן. מְקוֹם דּוֹד שָׁכַן. כְּרוּבִים בּוֹ שִׁכֵּן. חֶסֶד נְעוּרִים יִזְכֹּר: כִּיּוֹר עִם כֵּן. וְנֹעַם קוֹל דוּכָן. כַּבִּיר בְּיוֹם מוּכָן. לַנְּבוֹנִים יִזְכֹּר:

בִנְדִיבִים. כִּי הֵם בַּקֶּבֶר. וְלָנֶצַח שִׁמְךָ לְזִכָּרוֹן: כָּל אֵלֶּה סְמָכוּנִי. וְרַחֲמֶיךָ בִּקַּשְׁתִּי. לוּלֵא הֵם תַּמְתִּי. וְאֵינֶנִּי לְזִכָּרוֹן: כִּי הֵם בְּרוֹעַ. עֶדְיְךָ לֹא בָאוּ. וּמְמוֹתְתְךָ בְּפִיהֶם. שָׂמוּ לְזִכָּרוֹן: לְיוֹם זֶה נִכְמַס. סְכַם הַשְּׁוּמוֹת. תְּחִלָּה לַיָּמִים. וְרֹאשׁ לְזִכָּרוֹן: לְהִקָּרֵא בוֹ. כָּתָב עֵט וְשָׁמִיר. גָּלוּי וּבָאוּר. וְיָדוּעַ לְזִכָּרוֹן: מָוֶת וְחַיִּים שָׁלוֹם וּמִלְחָמוֹת. צַחְצָחוֹת וְשֹׂבַע. בָּאִים לְזִכָּרוֹן: מַעַלְלֵי גֶבֶר. וּמִסְפַּר צְעָדָיו. נִשְׁכְּחוּ מֵאֱנוֹשׁ. וּלְאֵל לְזִכָּרוֹן: נִסְתְּרָה דַרְכִּי. מִי יָכוֹל שִׂיחַ. לַשָּׁוְא נִכְתַּב לִי. הֵחֵטְא לְזִכָּרוֹן: נֶגֶד פְּנֵי גֶבֶר. מַעֲשָׂיו יוֹכִיחוּ. וְיַעֲנֶה בוֹ כַחֲשׁוֹ עַד לְזִכָּרוֹן: שִׂיחוּ מְזִמּוֹת אֵל. יַחַד כָּל בְּנֵי אִישׁ. עִבְרוּ תַחַת שֵׁבֶט. כְּצֹאן לְזִכָּרוֹן: מִי סוֹגֵר

He remembers the noble tribes (twelve), the oath of the tribes, the wanderings of the tribes does He recall, to strengthen them. When He says that He will crush those who bear the heavy yoke, then He remembers as an atonement the destruction of the site of the Sanctuary. He remembers the foundation stones (forefathers), who groan in Egyptian slavery. The sucklings who praised the Lord at the Sea of Reeds, the promise of the covenant (the circumcision) and the statutes (of the Torah), His holy word, all these does He remember. The memory of those who live austerely (students of the Torah) and study His beautiful sayings, who with their lips provide a substitute for sacrificial bullocks, He does remember. When the books that announce what is hidden, are examined, He remembers in love the wonderful pair of brothers. He remembers the honour of the sanctuary, the place where He, the Beloved, did dwell, where He allowed the Cherubim to rest, the love of our youth He remembers. The basin on its frame, the delightful voice (of the Levites) on the Temple steps, the Almighty recalls them in favour of the discerning on the appointed day of judgment.
On Sabbath.

for remembrance. O Lord, in Thee do I trust and not in princes, for they are in the grave and Thy Name is for ever for remembrance. All these supported me but I seek Thy compassion, without it I should have perished and not survived for remembrance. For in spite of their strength, they could not plead for me before Thee, those in whose mouths is Thy greatness have placed it there for remembrance. For this day has been stored the sum of assessments, it is the beginning of days and the first for remembrance. On it there is read out what was engraved with a diamond quill, what was revealed and explained and known in remembrance. Death and life, peace and war, dearth and abundance, appear for remembrance. The acts of man, the number of his steps, though forgotten by men, they are to God for remembrance. “My way is hidden” — who could say that? In vain was a sin inscribed for me for remembrance. In front of man his deeds give evidence, his falsehood bears witness against him for remembrance. Proclaim the plans of the Lord, all men together, pass under the staff like a flock for remembrance. He remembers (Joshua) the son of Nun, and the illuminating words of him who comes from Yephuneh, (Caleb), may they be recalled in prayer so that their deeds should be remembered. When the destructive gleaming sword is drawn for grief, may He hear and remember the supplications of those He has favoured. He remembers the noble judges and the sign given by Samuel at the time of the wheat harvest. He heals the folly of the simple, so that it is no longer remembered. When the destructive gleaming sword is drawn for the four punishments, may He remember the nature of the judgments He gave them. May He remember the hymns of praise in which David, at midnight, praised the rules of the night, may He remember his song in the darkness of the night on their behalf. May He illuminate the nightly search by the fire of the night upon the altar; the law in which they study by day and by night, may He remember for their healing. He remembers the palace that was taken from me on account of my selfishness. May He no longer recall that it was laden with deliberate sins. When anger, as at the time of the flood, is aroused in destruction, let Him remember the month of Bul (the completion of the Temple) in compassion. He re-

the storm until their destiny arrives and they go forth for remembrance.
As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘God remembered Noah and all the beasts and all the cattle that were with him in the ark and God caused a wind to pass over the earth and the waters subsided’.

Perform wonders for the living lest they become like the dead; is then Thy truth in the grave for remembrance? Once Thou didst pity because of noble deeds; pity us now even though we are without deeds; wilt Thou not make for Thy wonders a remembrance.

As it is written in Thy holy words: ‘A memorial has He made for His wonders, gracious and compassionate is the Lord’. And it was said: ‘He gave food to those that fear Him, He will remember His covenant for ever’.

Turn, O God, to those who sit in the gardens (houses of study), listen how they speak of Thy law for remembrance. Let their work appear before Thee; though they eat the bread of anguish, their reward is with Thee in the book of remembrance.

text: כַּכָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי קָדְשֶׁךָ זָכַר לְעוֹלָם בְּרִיתוֹ דָּבָר צִוָּה לְאֶלֶף דּוֹר:

members the test of every creature according to measure and in the scales; when they have committed acts of rebellion and faithlessness, may He remember them, full of compassion. As to the good and the evil whose deeds and way of life should be requited, may He not remember them according to the severity of the law. He remembers life, how long their life shall be; for death or for life He remembers all the living. The noisy throng of creatures passes before Him like lambs; He remembers each according to his worth. He remembers poverty and wealth, need and plenty, vice and virtue; in judgment does He remember. The open and the hidden, building and tearing down, dearth and superfluity, does He measure and remember. He remembers those who should live sheltered in the wilderness or in settlements; to send rain and wind does He remember. To hear the prayer of the people that reveres His Name and to lead back the exiles does He remember on the day of the Tekiah. He recalls terror and wrath, battle and wars; the destruction of
On Sabbath.

As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘Then those who fear God speak one to the other and God listens and hears, and it is inscribed in the book of remembrance before Him on behalf of those who fear the Lord and respect His Name’.

The foxes (Egyptians), the destroyers of vineyards, planned to cut off from the vine its root and remembrance. They oppressed them (Israel) with hardship, they cried out to Thee and were saved because of the piety of the forefathers who had been inscribed for remembrance.
As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘God heard their cry, then God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob’.

In days of old Thou didst see generations in whom there was no delight. Thou hast let them vanish and perish without a remembrance. One generation hast Thou chosen from among a thousand and allotted them Thy words; for their sake in every generation hast Thou engraved them for remembrance.
As it is written in Thy holy words: ‘He remembers for ever His covenant, the word He commanded for a thousand generations’.
